Ear Lobe Repair Surgery in Bangalore for Split, Torn or Stretched Lobes

Earlobes can split after an earring tear, gradually elongate from heavy jewellery or stretch after large-gauge piercings. Repair surgery reshapes the damaged tissue so the lobe has a more natural contour. The exact repair depends on whether the tear is partial or complete, how much tissue remains and whether the patient wants future re-piercing. NeoSculpt6 plans closure to restore shape while keeping scar placement and future jewellery use in mind.

What Is EAR LOBE REPAIR SURGERY?

Earlobe repair is minor reconstructive surgery used to restore the shape and continuity of a torn, split or stretched earlobe. Scarred edges may be refreshed and the remaining tissue closed in layers, while larger stretched openings or irregular traumatic tears can require additional tissue reshaping to recreate a smoother lower border.

The exact technique depends on the amount and quality of tissue that remains, previous repairs, scar behaviour and the desired final contour. Future piercing is considered only after healing is sufficiently mature, and is generally planned away from the weakest part of the repaired scar where possible.

Assess the Tear, Tissue and Future Piercing Plan

The surgeon examines the size and direction of the split, stretched skin, scar tissue and symmetry with the opposite ear. Previous repair and keloid tendency are also relevant.

The consultation explains local anaesthesia, scar position, aftercare and when re-piercing may be considered. Re-piercing should not be placed through an immature scar.

OUR PROCESS

OUR EAR LOBE REPAIR PROCESS

The surgeon examines the tear pattern, stretched tissue, scar quality, remaining lobe volume and symmetry, and reviews previous repairs, infection and keloid history.

The repair is marked according to the type of defect and the contour to be restored, avoiding a notch at the lower border.

Local anaesthetic numbs the earlobe in suitable cases, after checking comfort, allergies, medical history and whether one or both ears are treated.

Scarred or stretched edges are prepared and the lobe is reconstructed in layers to restore continuity and a smooth, stable border.

The repaired lobe is protected and the patient is guided on cleaning, avoiding traction and recognising infection or wound separation. Heavy earrings and pressure are avoided during early healing.

Follow-up checks suture removal or absorption, wound healing, contour and scar behaviour, with scar care introduced when appropriate.

Re-piercing is considered only after the repair has healed and the scar is mature, placed away from the weakest part of the old scar.

WHO CAN BENEFIT FROM EAR LOBE REPAIR?

  • Patients with a Complete Split Earlobe

    A completely split earlobe may be reconstructed when enough healthy tissue remains to recreate the lobe margin, depending on the age of the tear, scar tissue, tissue thickness and the desired shape.

  • Patients with Elongated Piercing Holes

    Elongated piercing holes caused by heavy earrings can continue stretching and eventually split. Repair can reshape the weakened opening before or after a complete tear.

  • Patients after Gauge Piercing

    Gauge piercings can leave large stretched openings that need tissue reshaping rather than simple closure; the surgeon evaluates how much skin remains and what final lobe size and contour are realistic.

  • Patients with Traumatic Earlobe Tears

    Traumatic injuries can create irregular tears, tissue loss or asymmetry. Once the wound is stable, planning considers scar tissue, missing tissue and symmetry with the opposite ear. Active infection, uncontrolled keloid tendency or poor wound-healing risk requires additional planning.

Ear Lobe Repair Surgery is planned around facial anatomy, surgical precision, recovery and natural-looking results.

Ear Lobe Repair Surgery Cost and Consultation in Bangalore

Cost depends on one or both ears, simple split vs stretched-lobe reconstruction, previous repair and scar complexity.

  1. 01

    One Ear vs Both Ears

    Repairing one ear or both involves different amounts of marking, local anaesthesia, closure and follow-up.

  2. 02

    Simple Split vs Tissue Reshaping

    A clean split may need a simpler closure, while a stretched gauge opening or irregular traumatic tear can require more reshaping.

  3. 03

    Previous Surgery or Keloid History

    Previous surgery, recurrent tearing or keloid and hypertrophic scarring can make planning and follow-up more complex.

  4. 04

    Follow-Up and Scar Care

    The written estimate should clarify planned postoperative visits, suture care and routine scar follow-up.
